papers.title: Novel bioprinting method using a pectin based bioink
papers.abstract: One major challenge of bioprinting is to develop a viable bioink to act as an extracellular matrix. This study investigated a novel method for bioprinting using a pectin based bioink. Besides pectin, Pluronic <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{}^{\@setsize{\tiny}{7pt}{\vipt}{\@vipt}\textregistered}" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mml:msup> <mml:mi/> <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">®</mml:mi> </mml:msup> </mml:math> F-127 was incorporated into the bioink to obtain the desired shape during the initial bioprinting process at 37 <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{}^{\circ}" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mml:msup> <mml:mi/> <mml:mo>∘</mml:mo> </mml:msup> </mml:math> C. Once an object was printed it was treated with Ca <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{}^{2+}" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mml:msup> <mml:mi/> <mml:mrow> <mml:mn>2</mml:mn> <mml:mo>+</mml:mo> </mml:mrow> </mml:msup> </mml:math> (pectin cross-linker) to create the final tissue/organ structure. The results indicated that pectin/Pluronic <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" alttext="{}^{\@setsize{\tiny}{7pt}{\vipt}{\@vipt}\textregistered}" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mml:msup> <mml:mi/> <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">®</mml:mi> </mml:msup> </mml:math> F-127 is a potential bioink. Moreover, this methodology provides a novel and fast approach for bioprinting.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文不涉及AI，仅关注生物墨水的材料开发。
llm.why_not_core: No AI integration, no computational model, no decision-making; only material development for bioprinting.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种新的生物墨水用于3D生物打印。
summary_zh.method: 以果胶和Pluronic F-127为基材，通过Ca2+交联打印。
summary_zh.result: 果胶/Pluronic F-127可作为潜在生物墨水。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验验证了生物墨水的可打印性和稳定性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a viable bioink for bioprinting that acts as an extracellular matrix.
summary_en.method: A pectin-based bioink incorporating Pluronic F-127 was used, with Ca2+ crosslinking after printing.
summary_en.result: The pectin/Pluronic F-127 bioink shows promise for bioprinting.
summary_en.validation: Experimental characterization of printability and crosslinking.
